name: Yield Branding
tagline: Cairo one-man branding studio with fixed-price identity packages
description: Yield Branding is a small Cairo-based brand identity studio run by art director Ibrahim Wageeh. It sells productised identity work — logo, typography system, stationery, social assets, tone of voice, deck and full brand guidelines — at a published flat price with a one-to-two week turnaround and two revision rounds. The site itself is a tight minimal Framer one-pager with four case studies (VYRO, Apexify, Resida, Ultrava) and a Cal.com discovery-call booking. Useful mainly as a reference for how a solo designer packages and prices identity work.
pricing_detail: Brand package $2,400, ~1 week turnaround, 2 revision rounds. Brand Guidelines package quoted separately, ~2 week turnaround. Discovery call is free via cal.com/ibrahimwageeh/15min.
agent_guidance: Treat this as a pricing-and-packaging reference, not a design source: it is the clearest published example in this batch of a solo identity studio putting a hard number ($2,400) and a deliverables list on brand work. Pull from it when you are writing a services or pricing page for a small design practice and need real copy structure — hero, deliverable list, three-step process, testimonial row, Cal.com CTA. Do not cite its testimonials as social proof; the named people and studios are unverifiable and read like placeholder content on a young Framer site.
why_it_matters: A clean, honest example of productised branding — fixed scope, fixed price, fixed turnaround — which is rarer to see published than the work itself.

name: ToyFight
tagline: Manchester design studio; 47 case studies for Twitch, KFC, GSAP
description: ToyFight is an award-winning Manchester, UK design studio founded in 2015 by Leigh Whipday and Jonny Lander. It works end to end across Strategy (positioning, naming, tone of voice, brand guides), Design (identity, UX/UI, product, websites and eCommerce, motion), Development (front-end, back-end, eCommerce, WebGL, apps) and Content (campaigns, CGI/3D, illustration, photography). The site carries roughly 47 project pages — Twitch, KFC, Under Armour, Royal Caribbean, Hollywood Bowl, Cult Gaia, Senreve, GSAP and more — plus a news feed and a satirical merch store. It is one of the strongest craft references for high-motion, WebGL-heavy agency sites.
pricing_detail: No published rates; project enquiries go to newbiz@toyfight.co. Merch store sells low-cost joke items.
agent_guidance: Reach for ToyFight when the brief is a premium agency or brand site with heavy scroll choreography, WebGL, and playful copy — it is the top-tier motion-and-voice reference in this batch, and its GSAP case study is a hint that the motion you are looking at is GSAP-shaped, so pair it with GSAP or Motion rather than CSS transitions alone. Read the work pages through the sitemap (https://toyfight.co/sitemap.xml lists all 47 project URLs); the /work index renders client-side and returns an empty shell to plain fetchers. Do not try to copy its layouts wholesale into a shadcn/Tailwind build — the value is the tone, pacing and typographic scale, not reusable markup.
why_it_matters: A rare studio that ships both blue-chip client work (Twitch, KFC, Under Armour) and award-winning open-source-adjacent work like the GSAP site, with a voice that is genuinely funny instead of agency-bland.
notable_for: GSAP site — 2 Webbys and a Lovie
Twitch, KFC, Under Armour, Royal Caribbean
evidence: https://toyfight.co, https://toyfight.co/services, https://toyfight.co/connect, https://toyfight.co/work (JS shell), https://toyfight.co/sitemap.xml, web search for founders/location

name: Kree8 Studio
tagline: Startup design studio with public per-page and retainer prices
description: Kree8 is a small distributed product and brand design studio co-founded by Jay Dwivedi and Satya, with a team of roughly seven designers covering landing pages, branding, logos, mobile apps, web apps, social graphics and 2D/3D product animation. It publishes exact prices — a $5,149 landing page with priced add-ons for development and extra pages, or a $7,199/month all-inclusive retainer — and claims 130+ brands served, naming Contra, Cluely, Opptics, Terac, Timefun and Bags. The site is a Next.js build with Projects, Playground and Pricing sections.
pricing_detail: Landing Page Design $5,149 (15-20 days); +$2,799 development, +$800 per extra page, +$800 per animation. Kree8 Retainer $7,199/month, unlimited revisions, 48-hour updates.
agent_guidance: Use this as a pricing-page reference for a design studio that sells both one-off scopes and a retainer — the add-on ladder (development, extra page, extra animation, each with a number) is a good model to copy when you are building a services pricing table with configurable line items. The client logo strip (Contra, Cluely, Opptics) is the credible part; the '130+ brands' claim is unverified, so do not restate it as fact. Note that /projects and /work both 404 — only /pricing and /playground resolve, so any deep link you generate should be checked before you publish it.
why_it_matters: Publishing an exact retainer number and a priced add-on ladder is unusual for a design studio, and it makes this a concrete model for services pricing UI.
evidence: https://kree8.studio, https://www.kree8.studio/playground, path probes for /projects and /work (both 404), HTTP headers (Vercel/Next.js)

name: Drapz
tagline: Solo brand and web designer; flat fee, unlimited requests
description: Drapz is a one-person brand identity and web design practice selling flat-fee engagements with unlimited requests to startups and founders. Work spans brand identity and guidelines, visual identity systems, branding plus UI/UX, and design-and-development builds, with six shown projects: Fugitive, Radiant UI, Lumora, Kinect, Stomic Studio and Skillio. The site is a short Framer page — benefits, work, reviews, FAQs, contact — and no actual price is published despite the 'simple pricing, one flat price' claim.
pricing_detail: No figure published. Site states 'one flat price, no surprises' with unlimited requests; the actual number comes only after contact.
agent_guidance: Low-value as a craft reference — it is a stock 'unlimited design subscription' landing page, so only reach for it when you want the standard structure of that genre (benefit grid, work strip, review cards, FAQ accordion, single CTA) rather than any distinctive visual idea. If a user cites it as a hiring option, flag that no price, no legal entity and no designer's full name are published, which is a real diligence gap. Prefer Yield Branding in this same batch when you need a solo-studio example that actually names its price.
why_it_matters: Representative of the flat-fee solo design brand that Framer templates have made ubiquitous, which makes it a useful baseline for what generic looks like.
evidence: https://drapz.design, path probes for /work and /pricing (both 404), HTTP headers (Framer)

name: Oakline Studio
tagline: Two-page Framer site selling product design and Framer builds
description: Oakline Studio pitches itself as a premium design studio for startups and tech teams, offering product design, branding, websites and Framer builds delivered by senior designers. The whole site is two pages — a landing page and a book-a-call page offering a 25-minute call — with contact running through Telegram (t.me/tejashinduja). There are no case studies, no named team, no location and no published prices, and the single testimonial is unattributed. It is an outreach page rather than a portfolio.
agent_guidance: Almost nothing to mine here — the sitemap holds exactly two URLs and there is no work section, so do not spend fetches expecting case studies. Its only real use is as a minimum-viable studio landing page: hero claim, service line, single testimonial, one CTA to a 25-minute call. If a user is evaluating it as a vendor, surface that the sole contact channel is a personal Telegram handle and that no work, team or price is published.
why_it_matters: A useful marker of the floor for this category — a Framer landing page with claims but no evidence behind them.
notable_for: Framer builds as a named service
evidence: https://oakline.studio, https://oakline.studio/book-a-call, https://oakline.studio/sitemap.xml (2 URLs), HTTP headers (Framer)
